title: Tasks app: the 2.0 redesign
goal: Decide what changes in the redesign of a small shared task app before any code is written

brief.text: Phones first; the desktop layout follows
The yearly price may scare off small teams
Who owns a task that two people edited offline?

cards.title: Ship the new pricing page?
cards.tldr: Drag the divider: the left half is today's page, the right half is the redesign.
cards.what: A redesign of the pricing page: yearly billing first, the Pro plan highlighted.
cards.why: Pricing is where trial starts are won or lost; the page hasn't changed in two years.
cards.then: ← nothing changes. → the redesign goes to every visitor next week; the old page stays one flag away.
cards.reason: the highlighted plan doubled trial starts in the last test

cards.title: Which home screen?
cards.why: The home screen is the first thing people see every day.
cards.then: The chosen layout becomes the default; the other one stays as a setting.
cards.reason: most sessions are a 20-second check of what is due

cards.title: Teach the swipe gesture with a short clip?
cards.tldr: A 3-second loop on the first launch, muted.

video.caption: The clip as it would play

left.label: No clip
left.detail: A one-line hint under the first task

right.label: Show the clip
right.detail: Plays once, then a **Got it** button

cards.why: New users don't find the swipe on their own; half of them never try it.
cards.then: ← people learn the gesture from the hint arrow. → the clip plays once on first launch and never again.

cards.title: How dense should the task list be?

left.label: Compact
left.detail: One line per task, 9 tasks on a phone

right.label: Roomy
right.detail: Two lines, the note under the title

cards.why: The list is the screen people stay on longest; density decides how many tasks fit without scrolling.
cards.then: ← about 12 tasks on a phone screen, smaller tap targets. → about 7, easier to hit with a thumb.

cards.title: Ship the new date parser?
cards.tldr: It reads «next fri 6pm» and «in 2 weeks»; the old one needed a date picker.

left.label: Not yet
left.detail: Keep the picker until the parser has tests in 5 languages

right.label: Ship it
right.detail: English first, the picker stays as a fallback

cards.why: Typing a date is the slowest part of adding a task today.
cards.then: ← the date picker stays. → typed dates work everywhere; the picker stays as a fallback.

cards.title: Price Pro at $8 or $12 a month?
cards.body:
### What we know
| Plan | Price | Trial → paid |
|---|--:|--:|
| Pro today | $6 | 9.1% |
| Test A | $8 | 8.4% |
| Test B | $12 | 5.2% |

> At $12 we earn more per user but lose a third of the conversions.
cards.reason: it grows faster and keeps small teams
cards.why: The price decides both how many trials convert and how much each one brings.
cards.then: ← more paying teams, less money from each. → fewer conversions, about the same revenue in the test.

cards.title: Send the digest daily or weekly?
cards.reason: daily opens halve within two months
cards.why: The digest brings people back, but too many emails get it muted.
cards.then: ← one email every morning with today's tasks. → one email on Monday with the week ahead.

cards.title: Which free plan?
cards.why: The free plan is how small teams find the app; its limits push them to pay.
cards.then: ← more free teams, slower upgrades. → fewer free teams, upgrades come sooner.

cards.title: Keep the sync flow as drawn?
cards.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[Phone edits offline] --> B{Online?}
  B -- yes --> C[Push change]
  B -- no --> D[Queue locally]
  D --> B
  C --> E[Server merges by field]

right.label: Rethink it
right.detail: Last write wins instead of a merge

cards.why: Sync is where data gets lost; changing it later means a migration.
cards.then: ← we build the flow on the diagram. → I come back with a new diagram before any sync code is written.

cards.title: Share a board as a looping preview?
cards.reason: most chat apps don't autoplay a link preview
cards.why: A shared board is how most new teams hear about the app.
cards.then: ← a PNG, works everywhere. → a short GIF, heavier, some chats show it as a file.

cards.title: Store reminder times in UTC?
cards.why: Reminders that fire an hour off after a trip are the top complaint.
cards.then: ← reminders stay right across time zones and DST. → simpler storage; a reminder set at home fires at the same clock time abroad.

cards.title: Follow the phone's dark mode?
cards.why: Half the users keep the phone in dark mode at night.
cards.then: ← the app switches with the phone. → people choose once in settings.

cards.title: Undo a finished task with a shake?
cards.why: Finishing a task by mistake is common, and today there is no way back.
cards.then: ← shake the phone to bring the task back. → a toast with Undo stays for 5 seconds.

cards.title: A home-screen widget in 2.0?
cards.why: A widget shows today's tasks without opening the app.
cards.then: ← two more weeks of work in 2.0. → 2.0 ships sooner; the widget comes in 2.1.
